dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Adventure Challenge

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Duel

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I see that you're really good at cards...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: It's naive of you to try to beat me with this trick.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I seem to have made a critical mistake...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Card skills are like martial arts. In that case you ought to practice more.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Oh, you're here. I can see you've been on quite a few adventures recently.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: As it happens, I do have some matters that require an experienced adventuring hand to resolve.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: If you're interested, go look for Tiantian. I've delegated the task of distributing commissions to her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about you?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Me? Nothing's come up that interests me so far, and at a time like this... the Adventurers' Guild needs someone to hold the fort.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Alright, then. If you'd like to take this task on, go look for Tiantian. She needs to grow up sometime, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Well, are you here to brave The Chasm by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Chasm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's never heard of any commission like that...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, you don't know about the Guild's commissions yet? Sorry, that's my mistake.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Well, The Chasm has been closed for a long time now. No one can go in without the Qixing's say-so, not even the Adventurers' Guild.

choices.text: No special pass for you guys?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Well, we wouldn't dream of being a bother to the people at Yujing Terrace. It would be a counterproductive thing to do, messing with pre-established policy like that.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Even Ms. Ganyu, who seems like the most amicable of the bunch, would probably just smile at us and say "why don't you have some tea while you wait here?"

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: And then she'll leave you hanging for most of the day, until you start wondering whether she'd forgotten all about you till she was nearly off from work...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Hmph, and as we all know, Ms. Ganyu never gets off work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That certainly does sound like a very Ganyu-esque way of refusing.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Either way, this means that Ms. Katheryne isn't going to be giving out any commissions about The Chasm anytime soon. Instead, we've got to find more... convenient people to help us out in private.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Convenient?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Yes, like for example, miners from Huishan Hall, members of the Millelith, staff at the Ministry of Civil Affairs. They can get passes to go in more easily, and...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And... what?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Well... So what I'm saying is, O valiant hero who saved Liyue from the sea monster, yet seems to have nothing to do all day every day, surely you can talk to the Millelith on our behalf?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No idea who you're talking about.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'm talking about you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, she was definitely talking about you!

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Don't play dumb. Who do you think I'm talking about, Rex Lapis?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Alright, quit your bragging.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Whatever the case... You have our thanks for your help so far, and we'd like you to consider helping us again.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: It's fine if the timing isn't convenient for you. It's just that... If you do end up passing through The Chasm, please help me look for a fellow named Muning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Muning... Who's that supposed to be?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: He's a specialist sent to The Chasm by the Ministry of Civil Affairs. We've got some personal matters that need settling. You can ask him about it if you meet him there.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Just pass this message along: "You still owe Lan money for drinks. Don't you forget that." He'll get the picture.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Wait, hold on a moment! There's one more thing. If you take this commission up, just negotiate your payment directly with Muning.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Don't ask me why the arrangement is like this... We did this at the Ministry's insistence. Best not to question their decisions and all...

choices.text: I'll keep an eye out on the way in.
I'll have you know that I do some important work, you know.
They don't close one eye with you lot?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Ugh, these commissions again?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you... I was just looking through the various commissions that have come in to the Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: But honestly, they're getting more mundane by the day.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Ever since the Qixing have taken control of Liyue Harbor, the scope of the Millelith's duties has been expanding slowly.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Lately, people seem to prefer approaching the Millelith to help out with tougher commissions, as opposed to asking us.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: The commissions we've got now are all things like looking for lost animals, transporting cargo, delivering letters— you know, the like.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Like this one over here...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: "Our Ash's gotten lost out in the wild. It's a <color=#00E1FFFF>gray cat</color> with the following features..."

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Commissions such as these take time and effort, but they're... Never mind.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I'm not one to be overly involved in day to day administration of the Guild, but I can't just let us be swamped by these commissions.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: In order to get people to trust in our ability and assign us more important work...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: ...I believe that we must hammer out some commissions of greater difficulty.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: There was a commission that came in not long ago from someone who wanted us to deal with a wandering Stonehide Lawachurl.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: It's been shelved for the moment due to a lack of candidates who can take that creature down, but if you're up for it, why don't you help us settle this matter?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Great. We're counting on you, then — I'll remain here and continue selecting commissions.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: If we had more adventurers as capable as you around, we wouldn't have this problem...

choices.text: Do you have any other commissions?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I do, but those are all a bunch of trivial, menial tasks, all of which I still have to sort through. We'll just have to leave the Stonehide Lawachurl to you.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: If we had more adventurers as capable as you around, we wouldn't have this problem...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: *sigh* Seems like nobody can get to the bottom of it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The bottom of what?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: The clue! ...Hmm, perhaps "rumor" is a better word... a rumor about treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: There's an adventurer who said that he found a clue to treasure in the vicinity of Tianqiu Valley... But he tried everything, and simply could not locate the treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: In the end, he gave up looking and reported it to the Guild instead, and now the Guild is offering a reward for anyone able to solve this mysterious so-called "clue."

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Any adventurer who wants to give it a go can follow the clue and see where it takes them. If they solve the riddle and find the treasure, the Guild will offer a reward.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: But so far, nobody has found even a trace of the treasure...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Oh, well, if you think you're up to it.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: If you really are interested, there's no harm in giving it a go.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'll mark the location mentioned in the clue on the map for you, then you can go take a look.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Well, like it says in the adventurer's code, finders keepers!

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: All the Guild wants out of it is experience in solving riddles like this. That is the most important thing for adventurers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...You're amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: You think so? Well, I don't do it for any kind of praise or approval.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: But since I am branch master and all that, I guess I have to show I'm making an effort or something.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I jotted down some thoughts on adventuring back when I was looking for the sword. Here, take them. Maybe you'll find them useful.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: ...? Excuse me, adventurer. Please see Katheryne about anything Guild-related — I am not intimately acquainted with the workings of the Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: If you're looking for the Master of the Liyue Adventurers' Guild, I regret to inform you that, that would be me.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: By which I mean, don't expect any help from me on Guild-related matters. I avoid involving myself in such bothersome affairs.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: That is, unless you bring news about the sword.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What sword?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: My older brother's sword. If I find it, I can finally give him a proper burial...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: It's the only fitting way to go for a martial artist like him.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: It's a flat blade, sharp enough to slice an airborne hair in two. It's named "Unseen Razor."

choices.text: How did you become Master of the Liyue branch?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Ugh, why does everyone ask me the same question... I will make an exception for you, though, and give you the full story.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I used to be a mercenary. I joined the Adventurers' Guild so I could take advantage of their superior intelligence network and track down the sword.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I may not be very literate but I can read the word "sword." So I just took on every single commission that had something to do with a sword.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Then, just when I'd finished my eighth— Or was it my ninth commission? Anyway, I'd just finished it, and then word came from the headquarters in Snezhnaya that I'd apparently completed two S-rank commissions.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: ...And suddenly I found myself promoted to branch Guild Master. It was all very strange indeed.

choices.text: I'll let you know if I find anything.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Oh, thanks! I love meeting people like you who are up for everything.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I am grateful to you, newcomer. It looks like it was worth me joining the Guild after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Aight, don't drag this out.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: It's been a while since I saw you last. For any Guild-related matters, please talk to Katheryne.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have we met?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Huh? Don't tell me you've forgotten who I am? Luckily, I still remember you.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I'm the Master of the Liyue Adventurers' Guild, although I tend to avoid involving myself in Guild-related matters and other such bothersome affairs.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: All that interests me is news about the sword.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The sword? What sword?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: My older brother's sword. If I find it, I can finally give him a proper burial...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: It's the only fitting way to go for a martial artist like him.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: It's a flat blade, sharp enough to slice an airborne hair in two. It's named "Unseen Razor."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did you become Master of the Liyue branch?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Ugh, why does everyone ask me the same question... I will make an exception for you, though, and give you the full story.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I used to be a mercenary. I joined the Adventurers' Guild so I could take advantage of their superior intelligence network and track down the sword.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I may not be very literate but I can read the word "sword." So I just took on every single commission that had something to do with a sword.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Then, just when I'd finished my eighth— Or was it my ninth commission? Anyway, I'd just finished it, and then word came from the headquarters in Snezhnaya that I'd apparently completed two S-rank commissions.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: ...And suddenly I found myself promoted to branch Guild Master. It was all very strange indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll let you know if I find anything.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Oh, thanks! I love meeting people like you who are up for everything.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I am grateful to you, newcomer. It looks like it was worth me joining the Guild after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Aight, don't drag this out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, have you seen someone who looks like me?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Like you? ...Oh, I see. You're looking for family.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I haven't, no, but I will keep it in mind.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I've been separated from family before. I know how you feel...
